subject: DPF evidence & cross-border safeguard checklist for VitalBridge RFP
messages:
From: Elena Morris <elena@vitalbridge.io>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 12 Sep 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: VitalBridge RFP — DPF evidence & cross-border safeguard checklist

Hi David,

Thanks for the materials on the platform — VitalBridge is compiling the procurement pack and we need a focused set of controls and evidence for our legal/privacy reviewers. Specifically we are asking for: 

- A mapping of Redwood technical and organisational measures to DPF control categories (encryption, segregation, logging, subprocessor controls, KMS).
- Evidence that supports EU->US transfer adequacy for transient inference data: which safeguards (SCCs, transfer impact assessments, DPA annex) do you offer?
- Details on key custody: do you support customer-managed KMS/HSM? If so, what's the onboarding and rotation process?
- Log retention and audit export: schema, retention defaults, and whether logs can be exported to our SIEM.
- A short runbook for how Redwood routes requests across regions (can you pin routing per-customer or per-route?)

Our deadline for the RFP pack is EOD next Tuesday. Can you confirm what you can provide by then and what would need a short follow-up? 

Thanks,
Elena Morris
Senior Procurement Manager
VitalBridge Health

Attachment: vitalbridge-rfp-initial-questions.xlsx (spreadsheet with RFP sections)

Hi Elena — thanks for the clear list. We're happy to support VitalBridge on this RFP.

Quick summary of what we can provide by EOD Tuesday:
- A DPF control mapping PDF (redwood_dpf_summary_v1.pdf) that maps technical safeguards to the common DPF categories.
- An export control matrix (dp_export_control_matrix.xlsx) that shows where data is processed, default retention windows, and subprocessor tiers.
- A short runbook we can share as a markdown file describing routing and per-route pinning options (runbook_dataflow_playbook.md).

Outstanding items that may need a short follow-up call / targeted artifact:
- Formalized transfer impact assessment (we can provide a templated TIA; full legal-signed TIA takes procurement sign-off).
- If you require customer-managed HSM with on-prem key injection, that needs scoping with our Private deployment team (we can provide a KMS onboarding checklist by Wed).

I'll attach the two documents we have ready and loop in Marissa and Karthik for technical clarifications. If you want a short 30-minute screenshare tomorrow to walk through the matrix, happy to set it up.

Best,
David
Head of Solutions — Redwood Inference

David — appreciate the quick turnaround. A couple of clarifying questions from legal/infosec while we review the artifacts: 

1) For model routing: can you confirm whether a customer can force all inference for EU principals to remain in eu-central-1, and whether fallback (burst/beta) ever routes outside the pinned region?
2) SCCs vs DPA annex: do you provide a DPA annex that references the DPF control mapping and the mapping to SCC clauses, or do customers rely on standard SCCs plus the control mapping?
3) KMS: looking for confirmation whether Redwood supports customer-managed keys with BYOK in hosted mode (not just Dedicated/Private). If hosted BYOK is not available, please indicate in the matrix.
4) Logs: our SOC team wants the log export format (json/cef), and whether you support streaming logs to a customer-managed CloudWatch/EventHub/Splunk instance.

If you can include a single-line response for each question in the thread, that would help speed reviewers.

Thanks,
Elena

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Morris <elena@vitalbridge.io>
Cc: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 15 Sep 2026 16:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: VitalBridge RFP — DPF evidence & cross-border safeguard checklist

Hi Elena — thanks for the questions. Short answers inline below, and I attached the runbook link and a log schema excerpt.

1) Model routing: Yes — customers can pin inference to a specific region (we support per-customer and per-route pinning). Fallback behavior is configurable: by default we will not route outside the pinned region unless an explicit "allow-burst" policy is enabled. For Dedicated and Private customers we offer stricter hard-pinning.

2) SCCs vs DPA annex: We provide both. Our standard contract uses SCCs where required; for customers asking for more operational detail we offer a DPA Annex that references the DPF control mapping (we include the mapping as an annex that ties specific SCC clauses to our controls). The annex is available as a redlined exhibit during contracting.

3) KMS / BYOK: Hosted BYOK (customer-managed keys in hosted mode) is supported via our KMS integration for vault-backed keys (bring-your-own-key to Redwood KMS proxy). For HSM-onboarding (customer HSM or on-prem HSM injection), that requires Private deployment planning — we can provide the KMS onboarding checklist and rotation schedule (attached).

4) Logs: We support export in JSON and CEF formats and streaming to customer endpoints (CloudWatch, Event Hub, Splunk). Export is configurable per-route; retention defaults are 90 days for consolidated request logs and 365 days for control-plane audit logs (both can be extended under an enterprise retention add-on).

Links / attachments:
- Runbook (public link): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-Redwood-DPF-Playbook
- Log schema excerpt (attached in packet)

If you'd like, Karthik can be on the call tomorrow to walk through the runbook and matrix. Let me know a time window and we'll set up a 30-minute session.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Senior Product Security Manager
Redwood Inference
